text:
Blake Coleman's first season in Minnesota looks a lot like his best years in Tampa and Calgary: hard minutes, heavy forechecking, and goals from the front of the net. He has 7 goals and 13 points in 24 games, 44 hits, and his goals sit right on his chances (7 on 7.3 expected). Nothing to discount there.

The Wild are rolling with him. They've won seven of his last ten games, he had three points in Boston on Nov. 14, and he scored against Nashville three nights later. The one soft spot is that his linemates have finished about five goals above their chances with him on the ice, so the on-ice scoring will likely come down even if his own doesn't.

The process is why coaches keep wanting him. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.9 wins last season, 96th percentile at taking chances away, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.7 chances per 60 from the home-plate area, 87th percentile among forwards. He's 34 with two Cups. Watch whether he stays at 16 minutes as the schedule thickens.
